summary:
Our project brings the stories of forgotten space hardware to life through an immersive, interactive museum. Rovers, landers, and instruments left beyond Earth represent remarkable achievements, yet their purpose and scientific contributions can be unfamiliar to young audiences.

Visitors explore destinations, discover mission histories, and learn what each piece of equipment helped humanity understand. Cinematic visuals, sound, and storytelling create an emotional connection, while accessible explanations connect that experience to real science. A recurring “Unknown Signal” challenge invites visitors to identify missions through clues, encouraging friendly competition and continued exploration.

By making these stories engaging and approachable, the project aims to inspire curiosity and preserve the legacy of space exploration. It addresses **“Abandoned but Not Forgotten”** by introducing school-age learners to the hardware left behind and the discoveries that make it worth remembering.
details:
1. What does the project do and how does it work?

Forgotten Explorers is a bilingual (Arabic and English) interactive educational web experience that brings the stories of forgotten space exploration hardware to life.

The project focuses on spacecraft and robotic explorers that were left behind on other worlds, particularly Opportunity and Spirit on Mars and Lunokhod 1 on the Moon.

Visitors begin with a cinematic space introduction before entering an interactive 2D Solar System. They can explore destinations, select available spacecraft, and discover their mission histories through interactive storytelling.

Each spacecraft has a dedicated mission console containing its launch date, last communication, actual versus planned mission lifespan, distance traveled, scientific discoveries, and a first-person diary explaining its journey.

Visitors can also explore interactive spacecraft blueprints to understand how different components work, use a dust and power simulator to understand how environmental conditions affect solar-powered missions, and discover lessons that can improve future space exploration.

The experience also includes recorded Arabic narration, English subtitles, NASA imagery, a mission quiz, a historical timeline called Time Machine, and downloadable achievement certificates.

2. What benefits does the project have?

The project makes space science more accessible, engaging, and understandable, especially for school-age learners.

Instead of presenting scientific information through traditional articles, it combines visual exploration, interactive simulations, storytelling, and audio explanations.

Its bilingual support helps reach a wider audience, while the combination of narration and subtitles provides different ways to consume educational content.

It also helps visitors understand real engineering challenges, such as power limitations, environmental conditions, communication failures, and spacecraft design.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

Our main goal is to inspire curiosity about space exploration and preserve the scientific legacy of missions that are often overlooked.

We want younger generations to understand that a spacecraft does not lose its importance when its mission ends. Even equipment that has stopped operating can represent significant scientific discoveries and engineering achievements.

By transforming these forgotten missions into interactive stories, we hope to encourage students to explore science, technology, engineering, and space research.

4. What tools, coding languages, hardware, or software did you use?

We developed the project as a browser-based single-page application using:

  • HTML5 and CSS3: For the application structure, layouts, and visual presentation.
  • JavaScript and JSX: For application logic, interactions, animations, and dynamic content.
  • React 18: For building reusable UI components and managing interactive application states.
  • Babel Standalone: For transforming JSX directly in the browser without a traditional build process.
  • Tailwind CSS: For responsive styling and interface design.
  • HTML5 Canvas 2D: For rendering the interactive Solar System and animated visual elements.
  • Web Audio API: For cinematic sound effects, ambient audio, and audio mixing.
  • NASA Image and Video Library API: For retrieving real space exploration photographs and media.
  • Python and NumPy: For supporting the audio processing workflow and project utilities.
  • FFmpeg and FFprobe: For cleaning, mastering, and validating recorded narration.
  • Node.js and Playwright: For automated testing and checking application functionality.

We also developed Python utilities for local hosting and preparing the application for static deployment.

The project does not require specialized hardware. It runs through a standard modern web browser.

5. How is the project creative?

The project's main creative idea is to tell the story of space exploration from the perspective of the machines themselves.

Instead of simply showing photographs and technical specifications, we use first-person storytelling to help visitors imagine the experiences of spacecraft that explored distant worlds and eventually went silent.

We also combine several creative elements:

  • A cinematic introduction that transitions into an interactive Solar System.
  • Planetary environments and spacecraft illustrations.
  • First-person mission diaries with original Arabic voice recordings.
  • Interactive spacecraft blueprints that explain engineering components.
  • A dust and power simulator that demonstrates real mission challenges.
  • A Time Machine that allows visitors to explore missions through history.
  • An educational quiz that tests visitors' understanding and rewards successful completion with a downloadable certificate.

This combination of scientific information, interactive technology, sound design, and storytelling transforms a traditional educational topic into an exploratory digital experience.

6. What factors did the team consider?

During development, we considered several important factors:

  • Scientific accuracy: Using real mission information and NASA resources to represent spacecraft histories and discoveries accurately.
  • Educational accessibility: Presenting complex scientific concepts in simple, understandable language.
  • Bilingual experience: Supporting both Arabic and English to reach different audiences.
  • User engagement: Using interactive exploration, simulations, and quizzes instead of passive reading.
  • Audio accessibility: Providing recorded narration and synchronized English captions.
  • Visual experience: Creating an immersive space atmosphere without requiring specialized hardware.
  • Technical reliability: Supporting local media fallbacks, browser audio restrictions, and different navigation interactions.
  • Future scalability: Designing the experience so that additional missions and destinations can be introduced over time.

Ultimately, Forgotten Explorers aims to turn forgotten space hardware into meaningful educational stories and remind people that even when the signal disappears, the discoveries remain.
